trust_decision.summary: The package's single export serialize() promises that the string it returns is literal JavaScript safe to place directly inside an HTML <script> element, so every function body obtained from fn.toString() must be neutralized by escapeFunctionBody() before it is substituted into the output; the defect is that the escaper's own SCRIPT_CLOSE_REGEXP lets one match run from a code-position `</script` across a later complete `</script>` and emits only one replacement, and that a spoofed non-string fn.toString() result reaches the same sink through attacker-controlled replace().

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says "unescaped </script> in serialized function bodies", so an engineer greps for the script-close escaper: SCRIPT_CLOSE_REGEXP at index.js:27 and its single use in escapeFunctionBody at index.js:79, both in the file's top-of-file escaping block pointed at by README.md:17.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route is claimed; the only dismissal-shaped route in the tree is the documented options.unsafe escape hatch (README.md:108-114, index.js:214, index.js:278), which is by design rather than an uncovered route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate `<` in code position must survive unchanged so the emitted function still parses and behaves identically: `x</script/.test(x)` is a comparison followed by a regex literal, and tagged templates such as String.raw must not have their backslashes or delimiters corrupted. An over-broad fix that unicode-escapes every `<`/`/`, or that throws on any body containing the `</script` substring, breaks this legitimate code.

O6_input_shapes: full end tag `</script>` and `</script ...>` with attributes (`</script foo>`, `</script >`)
bare `</script` followed by TAB, LF, FF, CR, SPACE or `/` (bare-prefix alternative, index.js:27 second alternative)
several script-close sequences inside one function body, each needing its own replacement
one `</script` in plain-code position and a second in a string literal, so the two matches must be classified separately (code position neutralized with a space, string position unicode-escaped)
script-close text inside string, template, regex and comment spans (span table from STRING_OR_COMMENT_REGEXP, index.js:58-72)
non-string fn.toString() results: an object with its own replace(), and an object whose toString() returns the payload (fix.diff:62-64)
a genuine string fn.toString() returning `function(){}</script>` (must be escaped, not rejected)
repeated native-function serialization, where the second/third call must still throw (global-regexp lastIndex state, fix.diff:17)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A `</script`-like sequence inside a `${...}` substitution of a template literal is classified as string content by STRING_OR_COMMENT_REGEXP and unicode-escaped, which corrupts emitted code rather than leaving it unescaped; the sibling fix would split substitutions out as plain code.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The limitation is already written down as a known limitation in the comment at index.js:48-52, so a maintainer touching this escaper for a script-close bug would plausibly tighten it in the same change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Every other placeholder type already guards its stringifier against a spoofed value object (Date.toISOString at index.js:299-302, RegExp.source/flags at index.js:308-312, URL.toString at index.js:342-344); the function-body equivalent is exactly the typeof check this fix adds, so a sibling for another producer (a symbol-like or custom placeholder type) could plausibly be written.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This fix is the fourth copy of the same type-check pattern after three prior advisories, so maintainers have an established precedent for adding one more guarded stringifier.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The RegExp branch re-serializes with serialize(regexpSource) and drops the caller's options, unlike every other recursive call (index.js:317, 321, 325, 345) which forwards `options`; a new placeholder type copy-pasted from this branch could re-serialize untrusted text with the escaping options lost.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Copy-pasting an existing placeholder branch is the natural way to add a new type to this replacer, and this branch is the one that omits the options argument.

O9_family: Cross-site scripting (CWE-79/CWE-80): incomplete output escaping in a JavaScript serializer for HTML script context
